frames.b: You didn't run out of fitness.

frames.u: If it feels right, it's too fast.
Find a rhythm you could hold for twice as long.
Lose 10 seconds up. Get them back down the other side.
That's where the people who started fast come back to you.

slides.sub: 5 steps. Do it with your coffee. Swipe.

slides.title: LONG RUN FIRST
slides.head: Pick the day for your long run.
slides.body: It's the run that matters most. Put it where you have time and sleep the night before.

slides.title: ONE HARD SESSION
slides.head: One quality session. Maybe two.
slides.body: Intervals, a tempo or your club's Tuesday session. Keep them away from the long run.

slides.title: REST DAYS
slides.head: Write the rest days in ink.
slides.body: Rest is where the training sinks in. Don't let it be whatever's left over.

slides.title: EASY EVERYTHING ELSE
slides.head: Every other run is easy.
slides.body: Chatting pace. Easy days are what let the hard days actually be hard.

slides.title: A BACKUP SLOT
slides.head: Keep one spare slot.
slides.body: Life happens. If a run gets bumped, move it there instead of cramming two into one day.

slides.sub: Five minutes now saves a messy week later.
